newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Novus to buy 30 pct stake in Oman gas field.
newsitem.headline: Novus to buy 30 pct stake in Oman gas field.

text.p: Novus Petroleum Ltd said on Tuesday it had signed an agreement to acquire an additional 30 percent equity in the Bukha gas-condensate field in Oman from International Petroleum Corp of Canada for US$26.5 million.
The acquisition will take Novus' stake in the Bukha production sharing contract to 40 percent, the company said.

The production sharing contract area includes the producing Bukha gas-condensate field, part of the West Bukha/Henjam field, located mostly in Iranian waters, and some exploration properties associated with the Bukha field, the company said.
The agreement is subject to final approval by the Oman government, Novus said.
The acquisition follows a recent increase by Novus in its interests in Australia, where the company last month acquired a group of WMC Ltd assets, including seven license areas in Western Australia.
Novus also holds a portfolio of licenses in the Carnarvon Basin offshore Western Australia.
Novus managing director Bob Williams said in a statement the agreement underscored the company's ability to use cash flow from its producing assets to support a reinvestment programme.

"The company's strong balance sheet will enable Novus to finance this acquisition wholly with debt, and the strength of the asset will leave Novus both cash flow and earnings positive after debt servicing costs," Williams said.
The other partners in Bukha are South Korea's Lucky Goldstar Group, with 50 percent and Heritage Oil and Gas of Britain, with 10 percent.
Novus is the operator of the project.
The field's current daily production is about 4,000 barrels of condensate, 1,200 barrels of liquefied petroleum gas and 40 million cubic feet of gas, Novus said.
An existing offshore pipeline has the capability of handling 150 million cubic feet a day of gas, the company said.
The acquisition of International Petroleum's interest by Novus is the latest in a series of ownership changes at Bukha.
South Africa's Energy Africa sold its 10 percnt share to Heritage Oil a few months ago.
More recently, U.S-based Transworld, a private company, sold its 50 percent stake to Lucky Goldstar, which is the principal buyer of the Bukha condensate.
